analysis.title: Inside Commodities, October 30, 2026
key_insights: UK oil and gas M&A involving a UK target or buyer has reached $19.6B year-to-date versus $16.5B for all of 2025 (LSEG data), the strongest year since at least 2022. High prices tied to the US-Israeli war with Iran, a 78% headline Energy Profits Levy rate on UK upstream activity, and cost pressure in ageing North Sea fields are cited as drivers of further consolidation.

BP plans to sell its North Sea oil and gas fields (announced July). Analysts estimate the sale could raise $2B. Cavendish names EnQuest, NEO NEXT+ and Ithaca as possible buyers. The next bidding round is in December, and EnQuest's CEO has said he is interested.

Recent UK deals: Genel raised its offer for Capricorn Energy to $436M, outbidding DNO. Ratio Petroleum outbid Serica for Pharos with a $196M offer (30% premium). Gulf Keystone and ShaMaran agreed a $601M all-share merger. Ithaca agreed to buy three Suncor offshore assets for C$1.2B.

Shell said soaring freight rates added $5.4B to its shipping lease costs in Q3 versus Q2, a non-cash accounting effect that feeds net debt. Cumulative increases in the first nine months of 2026 were $8B higher than the same period of 2025. Shell expects lease costs to fall once Hormuz shipping normalizes.

TotalEnergies said freight costs rose from about $2-3 per barrel to around $25, the main reason for a $6/bbl reduction in its Q3 liquids price realisation versus Q2. Tanker spot rates hit an all-time high in early October as Middle East producers used shuttle services and ship-to-ship transfers to move oil out of Hormuz. Shell's CFO said Middle East to China freight is about 10 times the 2025 level.

Brazil re-elected President Lula over Flavio Bolsonaro, who fled to the US. The real fell as much as 13% the day after. Analysts expect continued soybean flow to China (Brazil supplied 75% of China's soybean imports in the first nine months), and cotton and beef exports should benefit from the weaker currency. Brazilian producers heavily hedged foreign sales by selling futures this week.

Brazil holds the second-largest rare earth oxide reserves. A US plan to access them is seen as facing hurdles under Lula, who is expected to open prospects to all investors and require more domestic processing. Serra Verde, the only large-scale Brazilian rare earth project, was acquired by USA Rare Earth, which secured $1.6B in US government financing for a 10% government stake.

Brazil policy backdrop: government debt reached 82.9% of GDP in August (highest since March 2021) and the policy rate is 13.75%. Farm distress is expected to grow given high fertilizer and diesel costs, and Datagro estimates local gasoline is about 35% below international prices. Ethanol blending is at a record 32%.

Malaysia palm oil output is expected at 19.8-20M tons in 2027 versus about 20.28M tons expected this year, as timely rains limit El Niño losses. Indonesia is expected to decline by about 2M tons (GAPKI forecasts 53.7M tons this year falling to 51.7M tons in 2027) and Malaysia by under 0.5M tons. Malaysian stocks hit unprecedented levels in September. El Niño is forecast to peak March-May 2027, and the 2015/16 El Niño cut Malaysian output 13.2% in 2016.

Reuters poll of 25 analysts: LME cash copper is forecast to average $14,012/ton in 2027, up 7.3% from the July poll but 3.8% below the current price. Copper is up 15% year-to-date after a record $14,875 in September. The 2026 surplus estimate rose 12% to 125,000 tons and the 2027 surplus nearly doubled to 92,000 tons from 50,000. Analysts are wary of US inventory overhang and overblown AI demand forecasts.

LME aluminium is forecast to average $3,001 in 2027 (down 2.4% from the prior poll) versus a current $3,071. Analysts expect a 2027 surplus of 410,000 tons after a 2026 deficit of 720,000 tons. Prices hit a four-year high in June on Gulf supply disruption and have retreated as Middle East supply recovers.

Zinc is the best-performing LME base metal over six months, up 24% year-to-date at $3,980/ton. The 2027 average forecast was raised 11% to $3,487, and the consensus 2027 surplus edged up to 165,000 tons from 161,000.

Lead (Andy Home column): LME three-month lead is about $1,900/ton, down almost 6% year-to-date, with funds holding large short positions. Total LME inventory fell from 502,600 tons at end-March to 407,000 tons. Singapore is now a net exporter. China imported 175,000 tons of refined lead in the first nine months versus 24,000 tons a year earlier, while Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks of 26,802 tons are the lowest since August 2024, and the Shanghai contract is in backwardation. Data centers account for about 8% of lead demand (Trafigura).

QatarEnergy is buying long-term US and other LNG to generate revenue from price spikes if Hormuz is disrupted. It signed 3 mtpa from Woodside's US facilities (20 years) and up to 4 mtpa from Cheniere through 2054, 7 mtpa in two weeks in total, and expects more, with Venture Global in advanced talks for 3 mtpa. Cheniere deliveries begin in 2031.

Qatar LNG status: production halted in early March after Iranian missile attacks, and force majeure is extended to the end of 2026. Two of 14 LNG trains (12.8 mtpa, about 17% of export capacity) were damaged, with repairs taking about three years. Full production could restart within a week of a peace deal, limited to about 83% of pre-war levels. The Pearl GTL plant should return by Q1 2027, and the 142 mtpa expansion plan is unchanged.

Indonesia will no longer let coal miners meet the 25% domestic market obligation by supplying off-grid (captive) power plants, to improve supply to on-grid utilities. DMO prices are capped at $70/ton for PLN and $90/ton for select industries, and uncapped captive sales were more profitable for miners. The APBI association wants clarification, and the timing is unspecified.

Dry freight tenders: Jordan seeks up to 120,000 tons of feed barley (offers due November 4) and 120,000 tons of milling wheat (due November 3). South Korea's NOFI seeks up to 138,000 tons of corn for February-March 2027 arrival, extending Asian corn buying while Chicago corn futures sit near multi-month lows amid a brisk US harvest.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 shipping lease costs rose $5.4B versus Q2 on soaring freight rates, a non-cash effect that adds to net debt. Shell expects them to ease once Hormuz shipping normalizes.
Freight costs rose from about $2-3 to about $25 per barrel, driving a $6/bbl cut in Q3 liquids price realisation versus Q2.
QatarEnergy signed up to 4 mtpa of LNG supply agreements with Cheniere through 2054 from Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi, with deliveries starting in 2031.
Woodside signed a 20-year agreement to supply 3 mtpa of LNG from its US facilities to QatarEnergy.
Venture Global is reported in advanced talks to supply 3 mtpa to QatarEnergy.
BP plans to sell its North Sea oil and gas fields. Analysts estimate the sale could raise about $2B, with the next bidding round in December.

sector_views.sector: UK North Sea oil and gas
sector_views.rationale: Analysts expect continued consolidation driven by tax advantages, high energy prices and scale needs, though the pace depends on the oil price outlook.
TD Securities and the Reuters poll expect prices to decline as Middle East supply disruptions fade, inventories rebuild and the market moves to surplus.
Forecasts are well below the current price, but LSEG expects only a modest surplus, with historically low inventories limiting downside.
Analysts raised 2027 forecasts but see a US inventory overhang and possibly overblown AI demand. The 2027 average forecast is 3.8% below the current price.

earnings_insights: Shell Q3 2026 (reported 10/29): shipping lease costs rose $5.4B versus Q2 (non-cash, added to net debt). The first-nine-months cumulative increase is $8B above the same period of 2025.
TotalEnergies Q3 2026: liquids price realisation fell $6/bbl versus Q2, mainly due to freight costs rising from about $2-3/bbl to about $25/bbl.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 82.6% in July and the highest since March 2021, driven by fuel subsidies and social programs. Lula's promised small-business debt pardons could add to it.
Among the highest in the world, making rural debt servicing more expensive.
Median of 25 analysts, up 7.3% from July but 3.8% below current prices.
Down 2.4% from the prior poll and below the current $3,071.
Raised 11% but well below the current $3,980.
2026 estimate up 12% from the July poll, and 2027 nearly doubled from 50,000 tons.
The 2027 outlook shifted from balanced in the prior poll to a surplus.
Up from 161,000 tons in the July poll.
A modest decline as rainfall limits El Niño losses.
A larger decline than Malaysia, leaving a supply deficit in edible oil.

risk_factors: A drop in oil and gas prices could deter UK North Sea buyers, per Oliver Wyman.
Hormuz disruption continuing: freight costs, Shell's lease costs and Qatar's LNG force majeure (extended to the end of 2026) depend on shipping normalizing.
US copper inventory overhang and AI demand forecasts that may be overblown.
El Niño intensifying, forecast to peak in March-May 2027, with forest fires reported in Papua New Guinea and Irian Jaya.
Brazil fiscal expansion, 13.75% interest rates and farm distress under Lula's policies.
UK Energy Profits Levy at a 78% headline rate and policy uncertainty.
vol_and_positioning: Funds are running large short positions on LME lead, according to Andy Home, while Shanghai lead is in backwardation and LME inventories are falling.
Brazilian coffee farmers, sugar mills and grain exporters heavily hedged foreign sales this week by selling futures after the election.
geopolitical: US-Israeli war with Iran, launched February 28, with Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil and LNG passes.
Iranian missile strikes on Qatar's Ras Laffan in March damaged two LNG trains. QatarEnergy's first North Field train startup in Q1 2027 requires a US-Iran peace deal.
Qatar's energy minister met Iran's acting petroleum minister twice in recent weeks to explore oil and gas cooperation after the war.
Brazil's re-election of Lula over Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro keeps close Brazil-China ties and complicates US access to Brazilian rare earths.
UK government approved the Jackdaw North Sea gas field this month and reiterated its commitment to oil and gas in the energy mix while holding to net zero by 2050.
Indonesian power outages and policy change to the coal domestic market obligation.

tension_points.bull_case: Electrification across data centres, grids, EVs and clean energy provides structural demand support, and analysts raised 2027 forecasts 7.3% to $14,012.
tension_points.bear_case: Demand narratives are stronger than demand realities (Julius Baer), US inventories form an overhang, AI demand forecasts may be overblown, and surplus estimates rose to 125,000 tons (2026) and 92,000 tons (2027).

tension_points.bull_case: China is importing record lead, Shanghai stocks are the lowest since August 2024, LME inventories are falling and the Shanghai contract is in backwardation, which pressures funds with large LME shorts.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is on track for a fourth straight year of surplus, the LME three-month price is down almost 6% year-to-date at $1,900, and warehouse churn dilutes the inventory signal.

tension_points.bull_case: Tax credits, scale advantages, high prices and the BP asset sale are driving more deals.
tension_points.bear_case: The buyer pool is small, policy uncertainty persists, and an unexpected fall in energy prices could deter buyers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An unexpected fall in energy prices could deter buyers, per Oliver Wyman.
